display.purpose: The homepage thesis only. One instance per page.

heading.purpose: Band headings on the homepage and h2 in documentation.

body.purpose: Human prose. Capped at a 68ch measure.

machine.purpose: Paths, digests, field names and values, command names, configuration keys, datum numerals. Never used for prose or as a technical costume.

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked labels on figures, ledger headings, and the specification block.

rules: Two tiers and no third. The signature is the datum cursor that tracks the level being read; orientation is grouped section entry and a root-only cross-document route fade.
Motion is additive. No fact is dimmed, withheld, or gated by scroll position or hover.

Nothing that carries a fact reveals: not the ascent steps, the ledger, the guarantee pair, the comparison artifacts, the command cards, any element containing a code block, or the first viewport. The limits never arrive after the guarantees.
The datum cursor runs only at or above 64rem, where the narrative figure is sticky, and its first appearance is a fade at the correct level rather than a traverse from zero.

Hidden initial states exist only under html[data-motion], set synchronously in the head and self-revoking, so no scripting, a failed script, print, or a missing IntersectionObserver renders the complete page.
prefers-reduced-motion removes interpolation, not information: the cursor and focus ring still mark the level.
Only transform and opacity are animated. Colour, fill, background, border, size, and filter changes are instant, and an animated rule is a scaled pseudo-element.
Every duration and easing comes from a token. No component hardcodes a millisecond value.
No scroll-jacking, no parallax, no shared-element route transition, no runtime dependency, no framework hydration.

extensions.northStar: Authority over durable memory is a capability the software does not have. The surface is the drawing that proves it: a sectioned structure whose only crossing enters from outside the frame.
rules: A hairline rule must separate two genuinely different things. A rule used for texture is a defect.
Tier colour owns whole regions, never scattered accents.
Every narrative fact is present in the served markup.
Gold is externally authorized reference data. Never truth, safety, or instruction authority.
Square corners, no shadow, no gradient, no glass.
No third-party font, script, or asset is loaded at runtime.
The mark keeps a five-unit authorization void and an external key stub entering from the plate edge. A contiguous Bronze-to-Gold stack draws an automatic promotion and is forbidden.
Tier colour is visible at rest in every context. Identity is never a hover reward, and a fill is never animated.
dos: Let a tier colour own a whole region when the region is about that tier.
Put the non-guarantee beside the guarantee.
Give scrollable code regions a focusable stop and an accessible name.
Keep both themes deliberate and contrast-tested.
donts: Do not use gold, or any tier colour, as a generic accent or success state.
Do not build a grid of equal icon-heading-text cards.
Do not put an eyebrow label above a heading.
Do not reproduce the poisoned fixture's instruction text.
Do not claim users, deployments, audits, benchmarks, or production maturity.
